newsitem.title: USA: N. Koreans keep U.S., S. Korea hanging.
newsitem.headline: N. Koreans keep U.S., S. Korea hanging.

text.p: U.S. and South Korean representatives waited on Monday to see if North Korea was prepared to resume a crucial meeting on peace efforts that was suspended last week.

South Korean spokesman Ji Won Suh told Reuters the two allies hoped to resume the meeting in New York at 2 p.m. (1800 GMT) but by 11:30 a.m. (1530 GMT) had not heard from the North Korean side. He said Seoul's delegation was willing to give the North Koreans time to obtain instructions from Pyongyang but "it would be hard for us to prolong it (the waiting in New York) endlessly."

In addition to promises of more food aid, Pyongyang was demanding a "more favourable gesture from the United States" in the form of a promise to lift sanctions on North Korea, but such demands at this point "cannot be fulfilled," Suh said.

The three delegations, headed by senior negotiators, met last Wednesday in formal session to hear the North's response to a year-old U.S.-South Korean proposal for four-party peace talks that would finally close the books on the 1950-53 Korean War by replacing the fraying armistice with a peace treaty.

Although that meeting was inconclusive, negotiators reported "encouraging progress" and agreed to resume on Friday. But the North Koreans, saying they awaited instructions from Pyongyang, never showed up. The meeting was re-set for Saturday, but they again failed to appear.

The three sides maintained contacts all weekend in hopes of getting the formal chief negotiators' meeting back on track. Peace talks, if accepted by Pyongyang's Stalinist regime, may not begin until June or July. China would be the fourth participant.
